stories.dek: I got a date wrong. My three earlier editions today all listed August new home sales as a report still to come, at 3pm UK. It was actually published by the Census Bureau on Thursday 24 September: 684,000 homes a year, 6.4% above July, though the margin on that figure is wide. Nothing lands at 3pm today, so the only scheduled US data this session was the 8.30am durable goods report. For a long-term holder the housing number itself barely moves the needle; the point is that the calendar behind this brief is now right. Next Census release: construction spending, Thursday 1 October.
stories.headline: Correction: August new home sales came out Thursday, not today
stories.short: New home sales were Thursday, not today

stories.dek: US shares opened up: the S&P 500 is +0.29%, the Dow +0.39%, the Nasdaq +0.35%, while smaller companies in the Russell 2000 managed only +0.13%. The reason changed overnight. All morning the market was rising on cheaper fuel, but US oil has since clawed back to -1.41% from -2.27% at lunchtime, so that tailwind is fading. What replaced it arrived at 1.30pm UK: orders for the kind of business equipment that goes into AI data centres rose 1.6% in August, three times what economists expected. For a long-term holder that is the more useful cause, because equipment orders feed company earnings, while a cheap barrel does not.
stories.headline: Factory orders for AI gear jump, and US shares open higher
stories.short: AI gear orders jump; shares open higher

stories.dek: The VIX, the market's fear gauge, is at 15.25, down 2.68% from Thursday. But it has turned direction since lunchtime: at 12:30 it was 15.09 and falling, its low for the day, and it has since risen about 1%. That is unusual on a day shares are climbing, and it means insurance against a fall got very slightly dearer rather than cheaper. On the BuyTrigger ladder 15.25 is still the normal band: under 15 is calm, 15 to 20 normal, 20 to 30 nervous, above 30 is where the system's buy window opens. It sits 0.25 above calm and 14.75 below that window, so nothing on the ladder changes today.
stories.headline: The fear gauge ticks back up even as shares rise
stories.short: Fear gauge up while shares rise

stories.dek: The headline from this morning's US factory orders report was nothing at all: total orders for long-lasting goods were $338.6 billion in August, down $0.1 billion, and shipments fell 0.2%. One line further down tells a different story. Orders for business equipment excluding aircraft and defence, the closest official measure of AI data-centre spending, rose 1.6% to $87.629 billion against the 0.5% economists expected, and July was revised up to +0.6% from flat. Reuters reports two straight quarters of double-digit equipment spending growth. For someone holding AI-chain businesses for years, this is the demand side confirming itself in government data rather than in company guidance.
stories.headline: Business spending on AI equipment rose three times faster than expected
stories.short: AI equipment orders beat by three times

stories.dek: Micron ($MU) is at $1,097.99, up 1.62%. What matters is not the percentage but where the low sits: $1,091.05, which is $10.01 above Thursday's best price of the whole session. Five times this week the shares jumped overnight and gave it all back once US trading opened; this is the sixth attempt and the first where the entire session has traded above yesterday's high. It happened on the morning the official AI-equipment orders number beat by three times, which is the demand Micron sells memory into. The test is the 9pm UK close: if that low holds, it is the week's first real breakout. Its results are Wednesday 30 September, 9.30pm UK.
stories.headline: Micron finally holds its overnight jump once trading opens
stories.short: Micron holds its gap at the open

stories.dek: Nvidia ($NVDA) is at $224.76, up 0.08%. It opened up 0.90% and has given almost all of it back; its low for the session, $224.66, is eight cents above Thursday's closing price. So the strongest official reading on AI equipment spending this year moved the memory maker sharply and left the chip designer flat. That is worth more than either percentage: it says today's buyers are paying for the parts of the AI build-out where supply is tight, not for the whole theme at once. For a long-term holder it is a reminder that good news for a sector does not arrive evenly. Watch whether Nvidia goes negative into the 9pm UK close.
stories.headline: Nvidia barely moves on the best AI spending news this year
stories.short: Nvidia shrugs off the equipment beat

stories.dek: These two have moved together for weeks because Blue Owl ($OWL) helps finance the data centres Oracle ($ORCL) is building. Today they split: Blue Owl is up 1.14% at $9.36, Oracle down 0.20% at $139.24, a gap of 1.34 percentage points, and Oracle had been up 0.46% at the open before handing it back within eight minutes. This is also the first edition in four where Blue Owl's price feed was fresh enough to trust, so it is the first time the split can actually be shown rather than guessed at. Neither company has filed anything new: Oracle's latest filing is 23 September, Blue Owl's 14 September, both re-checked this run.
stories.headline: Oracle and Blue Owl part ways at the opening bell
stories.short: Oracle and Blue Owl split at the open

stories.dek: Robinhood ($HOOD) is at $120.30, down 0.43%. Two hours ago, before US trading opened, it was $122.65 and up 1.51%, the strongest riser on this watchlist. That is a 1.92% round trip with no company filing behind either leg: nothing new has been lodged with the regulator since 24 September. Moves like this, up hard before the bell and down once real volume arrives, are usually positioning rather than news, and that is the useful read for someone holding for years rather than hours. It is the mirror image of Micron today, which did the opposite and kept its gain.
stories.headline: Robinhood gives back its whole early gain within minutes

stories.dek: The Japanese yen has strengthened through 157 per dollar, at 157.0490 and up 1.09% on the day, its strongest point since the week began. A stronger yen makes the cheap Japanese borrowing that funds a lot of global share buying more expensive, so it quietly works against a rally. At the same time the US Treasury still publishes only Thursday's rates, with the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, so borrowing costs have not improved, and Bitcoin is down 1.31% since lunchtime. Shares up on an equipment-orders beat, borrowing no cheaper, carry funding dearer: that mismatch is this week's real tension, and the 25 September rate row lands after 8.30pm UK.
stories.headline: The yen jumps past 157 while US interest rates sit still
